newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh five-year plan targets poverty.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh five-year plan targets poverty.

text.p: Bangladesh's top priority for its next five-year economic plan is the alleviation of poverty, State Minister for Planning Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir told economists on Friday.

He said Bangladesh, where half the 120 million population live below the poverty line, had to raise gross domestic product (GDP) growth to 8.2 percent by the end of the plan period from the present 5.7 percent. The plan starts on July 1. "Investment will have to be increased to 22 percent of the GDP from current 18 percent," the minister said. He also called for an increase in domestic savings. "At present the rate of investment from national savings is nine percent and in the next five-year plan that figure should be raised to at least 11 percent.
"If we can do all the things properly we will be able to destroy the poverty circle," Alamgir said.

The minister said the focus would change from the public to private sector, following the trend of globalisation of international trade and investment. In the fourth plan, the ratio of investment was 56 percent in the public sector against 44 percent in the private sector.
"In the fifth five-year plan the private sector investment share should be 58 percent against 42 percent in the public sector," he said.
